painPoints.headline: Does any of this sound
painPoints.body1: These six sentences come up in almost every conversation we have with engineering managers. None of them need to be true in 2026.
painPoints.body2: If you are an engineering manager, CTO, or technical CEO: you recognise at least three of them.

knowledge.title: Knowledge loss
knowledge.description: When your most experienced engineer retires, three decades of project knowledge go with them. Almost none of it is documented.

reporting.title: Reporting work
reporting.description: You hired your engineers to engineer. On Fridays they write reports, meeting minutes, and status slides.

requests.title: Requests and changes
requests.description: Technical requests and change orders reach the right colleague. They get answered when day-to-day operations allow it. Which is often too late.

searching.title: Searching instead of finding
searching.description: Requirements specs, meeting minutes, lessons learned: spread across five systems. What gets found is what someone happens to remember. Mistakes repeat themselves.

research.title: Manual research
research.description: Standards, patents, competitors: every research effort starts from scratch, and nobody knows whether it is complete.

competition.title: Falling behind
competition.description: While you are still checking whether AI is safe with your data, your competitor is already automating their development. The safety question has long been solvable: GDPR-compliant, hosted in the EU.

about.headline: 20 years of product development.
about.introText: You know the problem with consultants: some understand AI but not your development processes. Others know your world but bring someone else in for AI. With me you get both in one person.
about.mainText: For 20 years I worked in product development myself and led teams. I know where time is really lost in an engineering department, because I sat in exactly those places myself: in project reviews, in change loops, searching for that one report from three years ago. And AI has been my passion for years, not just since the hype. That combination is AImation: I translate between your engineering world and the AI world. You do not need an interpreter in between.

quotes.text: 20 years as an engineering leader in industry.

faq.headline: Frequently asked
faq.subline: Answers to the most important questions

items.question: What happens to our design and project data?
items.answer: Your data is processed GDPR-compliant in the EU and is not used to train AI models. A data processing agreement is a matter of course. Projects under confidentiality we treat as exactly that: confidential. Which architecture is right in each case, we clarify before the project, not during.

items.question: Are the solutions GDPR-compliant and legally sound?
items.answer: Yes, that is not an option for us but a starting point. We select tools and architectures so that processing takes place in the EU and is transparently documented. If a desired tool cannot deliver that, we say so and suggest an alternative.

items.question: Does this work with our existing systems, such as Microsoft 365, SharePoint, or our ERP?
items.answer: Usually yes. We connect to what you already have instead of building new island solutions. What is possible in each case, we clarify in the initial call. And if something is not possible, we tell you upfront.

items.question: Does this replace our engineers?
items.answer: No. It replaces the routine work that keeps your engineers from actually engineering: sorting, searching, writing things up. The expert judgement and the final sign-off always stay with the human. That is how we build every solution.

items.question: How quickly do we see results?
items.answer: The fastest path is the pilot: one single process, fixed price, live in weeks rather than quarters. After that you know from direct experience what AI delivers for you, and you decide on that basis.

items.question: What does it cost?
items.answer: That depends on scope, but you find out beforehand, not afterwards. Training and the pilot have fixed prices; the pilot is 4,900 euros for four weeks. For everything else you receive a proposal with cost and expected benefit, in black and white, before you decide.

items.question: What is the difference between automation and an AI agent?
items.answer: Automation follows fixed rules: if A happens, do B. An AI agent can go further — independently researching, evaluating, and drafting proposals. For example: reading a technical request, gathering context from your systems, and presenting a draft reply. The approval stays with your team.
